subject: Stability & graceful-degradation discovery — summary + next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@finflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2026 21:05:00 +0000
Subject: Stability & graceful-degradation discovery — summary + next steps

Hi Oliver — thanks again for the 30-minute call earlier. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned and can move to a short pilot. Happy to update if I missed anything.

What we heard (pain & impact)
- Repeated availability blips during daily peak windows (11:00–13:00 PT) — 3 incidents in the past 6 months.
- Incidents resulted in a mix of high tail latency (p95/p99) and partial request failures; business impact: checkout delays and increased support volume.
- Primary constraint today: single-region deployment and occasional GPU OOMs when context sizes spike.

Current stack you described
- Model serving: in-house inference cluster running an open LLM (2x A100-equivalent nodes).
- Cache: Redis for short-term KV caching of prompts/contexts.
- Orchestration: homegrown autoscaler; traffic routed through internal gateway.
- Observability: Datadog with custom tracing, but limited token-level cost breakdown.

Success criteria (you called these out explicitly)
- Target SLO: 99.95% availability regionally during peak windows.
- Max acceptable p95 latency: 350 ms.
- Graceful degradation behavior: fallback to a smaller model or alternate region automatically; no failed requests exposed to users.

Proposed pilot (next steps)
1) Technical pre-call w/ Ben (SRE/solutions) to review traffic shape and KV/cache configuration — schedule for next week.
2) Provide a 48–72h traffic replay in staging (we'll supply replay tooling & instruction doc).
3) Run a short staged pilot: test automatic fallback to a quantized model + cross-region failover; measure p95/p99 and failure rates.
4) Share a mutual action plan (attached) with success metrics and timeline; if pilot meets targets, scope a Dedicated reservation for production.

Attachments included: mutual_action_plan.xlsx, stack-diagram.png, security-questionnaire.pdf.

Open questions for you
- Do you have a hard SLA review deadline from procurement?
- Any regulatory constraints on moving data between regions?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the tech pre-call.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

---
Redwood Inference — Developer-first LLM inference (hosted, dedicated, private)

Subject: Re: Stability & graceful-degradation discovery — summary + next steps

Thanks, Jasmine — this is a good summary. A few clarifications and confirmations from our side: 

- Incident history: to be specific — outages on 2026-07-09 (model OOM during a batch job), 2026-09-21 (regional networking issue), and 2026-11-17 (unexpected tokenization spike causing latency storms). All were user-impacting for 5–25 minutes.
- We currently fall back to a smaller model manually; we’d like that automation.
- Procurement is targeting an SLA decision by end of Q1; we can be flexible on timing for a pilot in December.
- No regulatory blocking on cross-region data for now, but we need to log cross-region requests for audit.

On the pilot: 48h traffic replay + staged failover sounds perfect. Can Ben and your SRE team also validate that our Redis prefixing is safe to replay? I can share a sanitized traffic dump.

Appreciate the clear next steps — Oliver
